look_here_first: LOOK HERE FIRST: Find the mallow-like flower and, most importantly, a mature flattened disk-shaped fruit (schizocarp). Count the wedge-shaped segments (mericarps) and inspect their projecting points; do not identify this plant from a purple leaf blotch or flower color alone.

project_inclusion.notes: Texas state-level native; three qualifying target counties not independently certified. Internal scientific metadata, not default public badge.

morphology_keys.habit: Annual herb with spreading to upright branching stems; habit varies with disturbance and moisture.
morphology_keys.leaves_attachment: Alternate, petiolate leaves; lower leaves may be broader or lobed and upper leaves narrower. Variable purple marks are not diagnostic.
morphology_keys.flower_reproductive: Solitary five-petaled, mallow-type flowers with many stamens united into a central column; check calyx and flower attachment.
morphology_keys.fruit_seed: Flattened circular schizocarp breaks into approximately 10–19 wedge-shaped mericarps. Mature mericarp tips/spines are more decisive than flower color.
morphology_keys.stem_bud: Inspect leaf axils for flower and fruit stalks; note hairiness and alternate nodes.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Separate from Sida and Abutilon by mature fruit architecture and mericarp count/shape; a purple leaf center or pink petals alone cannot establish Anoda cristata.
